comments.body:
Spike, 2026-11-08 (Codex, from recordings and the harnesses' docs; no model called). Not a small change. The full write-up follows.

# Spike: what a blocked agent is asking

The adapters should supply explicit question text when the harness exposes it. Use the screen to
confirm whether a prompt is visible, not as a general source of question text. Permission prompts
should use a fixed label such as `Approval requested: Bash`; do not copy the command or its
arguments into the fact. This needs a lifecycle for questions that can arrive before the blocked
state, and is not the small single-fact change in the brief. No build is included in this spike.

## What each harness supplies

### Claude Code

`extras/claude-code/hooks/hooks.json` reports `blocked` on `PermissionRequest`, and on
`Notification` for `permission_prompt` or `elicitation_dialog`. The local recording
`corpus/claude-code-2.1.288/dialog-input.txt` shows `PreToolUse` and `PermissionRequest` for Bash;
`plan-dialog.txt` shows `PermissionRequest` for `ExitPlanMode` and a generic permission
notification. These recordings do not contain a captured `AskUserQuestion` hook payload or prove
its precise interactive event sequence.

The [Claude Code hook reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) documents `tool_name` and
`tool_input` on `PermissionRequest`. `AskUserQuestion` takes one to four `questions`, each with a
`question` string and options. Its `PreToolUse` hook therefore has the text, but it fires before
the tool runs: it is not by itself proof a human-visible question is on screen. Another hook or
non-interactive host can answer or deny the tool. A pending value must not itself mark the pane
blocked. The docs also say `PermissionRequest` can run for a background call that cannot prompt.
`ExitPlanMode` has a plan, not an `AskUserQuestion` question; do not present the plan as a
question. An MCP `elicitation_dialog` notification is a different kind of prompt, and the local
recordings do not establish that its notification contains the question. It needs its own capture
before an extraction rule is promised.

### Codex

`extras/codex/hooks/hooks.json` reports blocked on `PermissionRequest` and returns to working or
idle on later hooks. The recorded `corpus/codex-0.154.0/hooks.txt` shows a Bash approval whose
`tool_input.description` asks to create a particular file; Escape fires `Interrupt` without `Stop`.
The [Codex hook reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#permissionrequest) documents
`tool_name`, tool-specific `tool_input`, and an optional human-readable `tool_input.description`;
Bash's `tool_input.command` is the command. The description is not guaranteed and may repeat
sensitive arguments. No supplied recording establishes a hook payload or lifecycle for a Codex
question dialog, as distinct from command approval. Do not claim that `PermissionRequest` covers it.

### OpenCode

The existing adapter consumes `permission.asked` and `permission.replied`, tracking outstanding
permission IDs even for children. The 1.18.34 recording in
`corpus/opencode-1.18.34/plugin-events.txt` identifies a Bash permission; the JSONL beside it was
cut to fields the adapter uses, so it is not evidence that omitted fields were absent. In the
[1.18.34 permission implementation](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.34/packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts),
a permission request also contains patterns, metadata and an optional tool; those can include
command material and must not be copied blindly.

The same version's [question implementation](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.34/packages/opencode/src/question/index.ts)
publishes a request containing its question array and awaits a reply; its
[question schema](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.18.34/packages/schema/src/v1/question.ts)
defines `question.asked`, `question.replied` and `question.rejected`, with a question string and
request id. The current `extras/opencode/plugin/muster.js` ignores those events, including from
child sessions. These are source-backed fields, not a recorded live question in this repo. The
adapter needs to track both questions and permissions by request id, handle simultaneous requests
and child sessions, and clear or select another pending request when one is answered or rejected.
A replay of only the last fact is insufficient.

## Recommended shape and source

Use `AgentFacts.other["blocked_question"]`, already sent in the daemon's pane record and
`PaneStateChanged.facts.other`, and already available in `muster window --json` under `facts.other`.
No daemon or shell protocol field is required for this shape. The flag is
`--fact blocked_question=TEXT`; a blank value clears it. Facts are limited to 256 UTF-8 bytes and
reject control characters (`crates/muster-daemon/src/facts.rs`). Normalize all whitespace to
single spaces, remove or replace other control characters, and truncate at a UTF-8 character
boundary to at most 256 bytes, with an ellipsis included in that limit. Prefer the first question
of the oldest visible pending request. Show no text when no trusted explicit question is known;
the current subtitle remains the fallback. The exact ordering should follow the visible dialog if
the harness supplies that order, rather than guessing from a subagent's arrival.

A pending question received before its dialog is rendered needs a distinct lifetime from the
currently visible one. Promote it only when the matching prompt is established; clear it when the
question is answered, rejected or interrupted, on a session change, and when the daemon's effective
state leaves blocked. If a second prompt remains, select and publish that one instead of clearing
all. The detector can briefly publish working after a key even if the dialog remains or another is
about to draw (`crates/muster-detect/src/detector/tests.rs`, dialog answered cases), so clearing the
only copy on that transient loses the still-pending question. Conversely, keeping it without a
request identity can show an old question when a different prompt blocks. The daemon processes
facts before the state report and the detector confirms blocked asynchronously
(`crates/muster-daemon/src/session.rs`, `report`); clearing every fact whenever the current state is
not blocked also discards a question reported just before its first blocked state.

The report CLI's `--from` supports a fixed list of flags and does not support arbitrary `--fact`
(`crates/muster-daemon/src/report.rs`, `FROM_FLAGS`). Extracting and safely normalizing a question
from hook JSON therefore needs a new supported input path or adapter code; it cannot be expressed
as `--from fact=...` today. `other` is part of the daemon API as well as the CLI, and it is held in
the live pane record. `persist.rs` excludes agent facts from the on-disk arrangement. The build
must verify that no new log records include the text or full hook input.

## Screen fallback

Detection already reads terminal cells and identifies blocked screens. Its manifest result gives a
state and rule, and some rules supply fixed `shows` or `waiting` text; it does not extract a
question from a blocked rule. The prompt extractor is for a composer's typed text, not arbitrary
question bodies. `claude.toml`, `codex.toml` and `opencode.toml` match different dialog chrome and
some text wraps across screen widths. Extracting a question would require new per-harness regions,
wrap handling and detection tests, and could copy terminal output or a command containing secrets.
For an agent without a usable adapter, retain the subtitle instead of guessing from the screen.

## Command and question privacy

Never publish a permission request's raw command, shell fragment, argument list, path, environment,
metadata, or model-provided description. Truncation or regex masking is not a reliable way to
identify every token or secret: show a fixed generic label, optionally with an allowlisted tool
category, and leave unknown tool names generic. Do not write these inputs, the extracted question,
or the full fact into the run log. Test this with a synthetic secret in commands and descriptions.

An explicit question itself can contain private text. Showing it in the strip and exposing it via
`window --json` and the daemon API is intentional for this feature; it is not guaranteed free of
secrets. Treat it as content from the pane, not safe metadata. A report path that builds
`--fact KEY=VALUE` as an OS argument also exposes that value to process inspection on systems that
allow it; prefer a bounded stdin-based report path rather than putting extracted content in a
child process argument. Verify that logs, errors, snapshots and any IPC diagnostics do not write
the text, and document the deliberate API exposure.

## Why stop at the spike

An adapter-to-fact path exists, but the correct lifecycle needs pending request identity, a way to
join early hook data to the detector's effective state, OpenCode question handling alongside its
multiple permission IDs, and validation against real question recordings. Screen fallback is its
own detection feature. Those changes are larger than the brief's small report-and-field build and
the available recordings do not establish Claude's or Codex's question-dialog event sequence.
No model was called. A future build should add recorded or otherwise authoritative fixtures before
claiming these flows, exercise interruption and overlapping prompts, and verify redaction and
absence from logs. No daemon protocol change is proposed for the fact map; if review chooses a
separate daemon field instead, assign its tag and next protocol minor and review it before building.

comments.body: Owner, 2026-11-09, after hearing the spike's findings (each harness reports differently, live recordings needed, question text can carry private material): not now. "I'm okay with, for now not doing that kind of hard to achieve vision. It doesn't seem super important. We can do something that's a bit more robust and reliable." The blocked card keeps the pane's subtitle. A possible later step: a label for the kind of stop (a question vs an approval) without its text.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A Needs you card for a blocked agent is most useful when it shows what the agent is asking, as the mock-up does ("Which locations should your starting rules let it clear?", Lectern page muster-ui-redesign). Nothing in proto/muster.proto carries that today.

Two likely sources: the harness adapters, since a Claude Code hook sees the tool call an agent is blocked on, including an AskUserQuestion call's questions; and the screen, which the daemon already reads to classify state. The strip ships without this and gains it later.
title: Pass on what a blocked agent is asking, for the Needs you strip
